description: Figure: nucleotide-site occlusion in the superposed LRGUK GUK-like domain against active guanylate kinase controls
code:
import numpy as np, json, pandas as pd, matplotlib.pyplot as plt
df=pd.read_csv("out/ligand_contacts.csv")
fig=plt.figure(figsize=(15,8.5)); gs=fig.add_gridspec(1,2,width_ratios=[1.9,1],wspace=0.3)

# Panel A: ligand-contact residues, GK vs LRGUK
ax=fig.add_subplot(gs[0])
d=df.copy().reset_index(drop=True)
y=np.arange(len(d))[::-1]
ax.barh(y+0.19, d.GK_mindist, height=0.36, color="#2e7d5b", label="mouse GUK1 (1LVG) residue to ligand")
ax.barh(y-0.19, d.LRGUK_mindist, height=0.36, color="#d94a3d", label="superposed LRGUK residue to ligand")
ax.set_yticks(y)
ax.set_yticklabels([f"{r.ligand}  {r.GK_res} -> {r.LRGUK_res}" for _,r in d.iterrows()],fontsize=8.5)
ax.axvline(2.5,ls="--",c="k",lw=1)
ax.text(2.55,len(d)-1.5,"2.5 A: steric overlap",fontsize=9,rotation=90,va="top")
ax.set_xlabel("minimum heavy-atom distance to the bound GMP or ADP (A)",fontsize=10)
ax.set_title("A. Nucleotide-site residues of guanylate kinase and their LRGUK counterparts\n"
             "after Kabsch superposition (160 CA pairs, RMSD 1.33 A)",fontsize=11,loc="left")
ax.legend(fontsize=9,loc="lower right",frameon=False)
for s in ("top","right"): ax.spines[s].set_visible(False)

# Panel B: clash counts vs active-GK control
ax2=fig.add_subplot(gs[1])
models=["AF human GUK1\n(active control)","mouse GUK1 1LVG\n(self, control)","AF LRGUK\nGUK-like domain"]
gmp=[2,0,11]; adp=[1,0,21]
x=np.arange(3); w=0.36
ax2.bar(x-w/2,gmp,w,color="#3b6ea5",label="GMP site")
ax2.bar(x+w/2,adp,w,color="#e8a33d",label="ADP site")
for i,(a,b) in enumerate(zip(gmp,adp)):
    ax2.text(i-w/2,a+0.4,str(a),ha="center",fontsize=10); ax2.text(i+w/2,b+0.4,str(b),ha="center",fontsize=10)
ax2.set_xticks(x); ax2.set_xticklabels(models,fontsize=9)
ax2.set_ylabel("protein heavy atoms within 2.5 A\nof the bound nucleotide position",fontsize=10)
ax2.set_title("B. Both nucleotide sites of LRGUK are\nfilled by side chains",fontsize=11,loc="left")
ax2.legend(fontsize=9,frameon=False)
for s in ("top","right"): ax2.spines[s].set_visible(False)
plt.show()
print(d.to_string(index=False))
